note: Adversarial relay (anti-sycophancy §2 mechanism 1: 'Separate contexts + adversarial relay. The opponent's message is injected as Your opponent argued: «…». Rebut it. — NOT as an agreeable peer turn'). NEW MODULE packages/core/src/agent_debate/core/agents/relay.py. build_adversarial_relay(opponent_message, *, run_id=None) -> str FIRST sanitises the opponent message through the security gatekeeper (agent_debate.core.security.sanitize_untrusted_text — normalise + injection-neutralise + length-cap; opponent text is another agent's untrusted output, §5.7 defence-in-depth) and only THEN wraps the sanitised text in the single named template ADVERSARIAL_RELAY_TEMPLATE = 'Your opponent argued: «{message}». Rebut it.' (the '«»' guillemets live once here, never re-inlined). RELAY_SANITISE_SOURCE='opponent_relay' labels the sanitiser's optional log event. relay_opponent_turn(context, side, opponent_message, *, max_words=None, run_id=None) -> str frames the message then REUSES anchoring.anchor_turn(..., opponent_message=framed) so the side anchor + framed relay combine into ONE user turn appended to the agent's OWN AgentContext (DRY — no duplicated anchor logic). CRITICAL invariants pinned by tests: the relay enters the agent's own context as a USER turn (an untrusted prompt to rebut), NEVER an assistant turn, and NEVER appended to the opponent's thread (5.4 isolation — opponent history stays empty). Framing is adversarial (contains 'Rebut it'), not an agreeable peer/assistant turn (no 'you agree'/'assistant:'/'peer'). Logs via LOG (get_logger('agents') -> adversarial_relay_injected with identity+side). API gatekeeper (Epic 13): N/A — pure text + container mutation, no agent and no network call (the security gatekeeper is pure text processing). No hard-coded values: framing template + sanitiser source are named constants; sanitisation reuses the existing gatekeeper.
